sources.entry: MarketMirror - Tests ads, prices, emails and sales pitches on simulated buyers and returns a go / iterate / no-go report; runs locally from coding agents as an MCP server. #free #opensource

summary.one_liner: MarketMirror is a self-hosted, open-source tool that tests ads, prices, emails, website journeys and sales pitches on LLM-simulated buyer personas and returns a go / iterate / no-go report, runnable from AI coding agents via MCP.
keywords: test ideas before spending on ads
summary.what_it_does: MarketMirror generates AI-written buyer personas from an audience spec, each with a background, budget, phone and data situation, trust concerns and a decision card. It places ads among organic posts in simulated Facebook, Instagram, Reddit, TikTok, LinkedIn and X feeds and records actions such as clicks, hides and comments. It surveys the personas with free-text answers converted to 1-5 ratings, runs split tests of messages, asks Van Westendorp price questions, and rehearses a sales pitch with objections and rebuttals. It can also send simulated visitors through a website, test emails without sending them, and run optional social rounds on OASIS. Results are written to a self-contained HTML dashboard with exports to Markdown, JSON, CSV and PDF. The README also describes optional calibration against real campaign exports and backtests.
use_cases: pre-test ads before spending on a live campaign
rehearse a sales pitch and objection handling
compare pricing or trial offers with simulated buyers
test subject lines and email sequences
find where website visitors drop off
pick which audience or country to start with
how_to_run: claude mcp add market-mirror -- uvx marketmirror (or any MCP client: command uvx, args ["marketmirror"])
stack: LLM providers of the user's choice (including Claude, Codex, Gemini)
notable: Runs from coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor) as an MCP server, and is listed in the official MCP Registry
Survey answers are rated with semantic similarity rating using local embeddings, avoiding extra model calls
Buyers keep memory across tests in the same run, so an earlier ad reaction carries into the later pitch
Mixed-provider markets let different LLM providers write and play their own share of the personas, with dashboard comparison
Dashboard is one offline HTML file with a table behind every chart; the README shows a worked example with simulated results
caveats: The buyers are AI-generated; the README states results describe simulated cohorts and are not forecasts of real demand or proof of predictive accuracy.
Requires Linux, macOS or WSL, plus Git, uv and Python 3.12; quick start makes paid-or-quota model calls on the chosen provider.
Large runs can hit provider usage limits; the README's 3,000-person run took hours and needed a switch to API keys mid-run.
